issues.legal_issue: An error in allowing excessive deductions after considering fully disclosed claims is an under-assessment, not an escaped assessment, and may be corrected through revisional jurisdiction.
material_facts: The assessee fully disclosed the income and claimed deductions for maintaining immature plantations.
The assessing officer considered the deduction claims and allowed some deductions, but the Commissioner considered the amounts allowed excessive and directed fresh disposal.
issues.conclusion: The case was not one of escaped assessment, and the Commissioner had jurisdiction to make the revisional order.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 confers revisional power, subject to the Act, while section 35 provides the procedure for income escaping assessment. Every case of under-assessment is not a case of escaped assessment. The Court followed Deputy Commissioner of Agricultural Income-tax and Sales Tax v. Dhanalakshmi Vilas Cashew Co. and distinguished Maharajadhiraj Sir Kameshwar Singh v. State of Bihar and Kamal Singh v. Commissioner of Income-tax, which concerned income omitted from assessment rather than a considered deduction claim.

rule.if: revision_proceeding and income_fully_disclosed and deduction_claim_considered and excessive_deduction_allowed

predicates.revision_proceeding: An authority is reviewing an assessment through a revisional proceeding.
predicates.income_fully_disclosed: The assessee disclosed the income relevant to the assessment.
predicates.deduction_claim_considered: The assessing officer considered the assessee's claim for deductions.
predicates.excessive_deduction_allowed: The assessing officer allowed deductions in an amount later considered excessive.

issues.definition: When a revisional proceeding concerns fully disclosed income and deductions that the assessing officer considered but allowed excessively, the revisional authority has jurisdiction.
